objective: Evaluate the effect of the Nucleus invention on the Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) of ECG signals
independent_variables: presence of conductive mesh in electrode gel
controls: standard electrode gel without conductive mesh
baseline: ECG signals from a standard electrode gel without conductive mesh
procedure: Recruit 20 healthy adults and obtain informed consent
Record ECG signals from each participant using both the standard electrode gel and the Nucleus invention
Administer a 30-minute exercise protocol to each participant
Record ECG signals from each participant after the exercise protocol
expected_result: A 15.2% improvement in SNR of ECG signals when using the Nucleus invention compared to the standard electrode gel
falsification_condition: Failure to achieve a statistically significant increase in SNR (p < 0.05) when compared to the baseline condition
sample_requirements: 20 healthy adults aged 18-40 with no history of cardiovascular disease
safety_constraints: Ensure that all participants are comfortable and able to complete the exercise protocol without any adverse effects
information_gain: Understanding the effect of the Nucleus invention on the SNR of ECG signals and its potential applications in medical devices
